First True Vietnam Phở Experience
Feb 2019 • Solo
After a lengthy travel from one side of the world to the other, what I needed even more than rest was a soothing bowl of phở. Pho Hung came highly recommended and was conveniently just a few blocks from my hostel. Being from Canada/Australia, I've eaten a lot of quality pho, so I wanted my first in Vietnam to be special. I'm pleased to say my expectations were met from the minute I walked in off the hectic street past the lineup of motorbikes out front. I was promptly seated at a communal table at the back next to a friendly group who spoke English and welcomed me to Vietnam and were keen to show me the proper way to eat pho. I already had the ritual down pat, but was curious to know what all the impressive herbs were. Half of which, like saw-tooth coriander, I'd never encountered in real life at any pho joint back home. Visually, that's what I found instantly most impressive, in addition to the bright orange dipping sauce that was also a new addition for me. This wouldn't be my last time eating here either. I'd return at least two more times. I later discovered there were other locations in what was a chain of pho restaurants. My first order was a basic beef pho, but I got more adventurous with each visit, opting for a variety with cartilage which I wasn't super keen on. But the beef and brisket were always very tasty and sliced to just the right thickness with the perfect amount of texture and consistency. The broth was exceptional. I didn't sully it with any sauce, rather tasted it unspoilt with a spoon and slurped it all up at the end. Naturally, I ordered a ca phe sua da each time. The iced coffee was a bit thick and chocolatey, which my sweet tooth didn't mind, but I had much better elsewhere. In subsequent visits, I also brought my own napkins as this was something I realised was often missing at simple eateries. That's when I discovered you can save a couple thousand dong by not opening the wet nappies provided. Pho Hung proved to be a solid initiation into the world of pho in Vietnam. Though it wouldn't be the best I'd eat, it served as the benchmark to which I would compare every other bowl of pho.

Having a bowl of so so Pho without trying the good ones is super satisfying as one has not much of expectation. But once you’ve tried a good one then it’s really hard to match it.

Just make sure you go to the right one as there’s another Pho Hung (same name but different owner or not a real franchise). As long as its clean, it tastes better than cheap.
Sep 2014 • Couples
This is a popular Saigon pho franchise that specialises in beef noodle soup, also known locally as pho. Their consistent recipe & high cleanliness standards make the several Pho Hung restaurants around HCMC very popular with the local middle-class. After my first sip of their famous broth i thought it was $3.00 USD pocket-change well spent.
 
Dirty pots & dodgy-looking cooks are typical of small local businesses however the kitchens at Pho Hung are located at the front of the restaurants in full view. The hygiene standards at Pho Hung are laid bare showing a very clean workbench, I saw the workstation constantly wiped clean & clear of food & grime. Stretching the friendship I stood in front of this kitchen area on my first visit looking at the big steaming pot of broth with which the whole operation is dependent on...yes, I was also trying to steal their recipe too. As a fan of the good pho I was glad to see this pho kitchen set-up at Pho Hung & was happy to see the person preparing my meal was no shady looking pirate but a presentable lady who even wore a hair net & white overalls.
 
The Pho Hung franchises are all enclosed from the outside & air-conditioned. They use Pho Hung-branded cutlery & staff wear franchise yellow buttoned shirts & are generally presentable in that casual Vietnamese way. Most pho restaurants serve pho with a small dish of mint leaves & bean sprouts however here they provide a large plate full of green mints. Chopsticks are clean & each pair is wrapped in plastic sleeve after washing. There is a good amount of meat, relative to Vietnamese restaurants. Quality of beef is very good, no sinew, fatty pieces or off-cuts for the standard Beef noodle soup. Fresh egg noodle is used & is ok but in my opinion, the noodles in foreign countries are more silky & soft probably due to higher quality ingredients. The broth….is clear, sweet & tasty. The same goes for its fragrance, no foul poultry smell or anything unusual for a bowl of pho. The cook uses a lot of chopped sweet onion but that is to enhance the flavour. I believe there is MSG used in the recipe which is normal for Asian broths, the question is how much do they use? What do they say...ignorance is bliss.
 
Price-wise a bowl of pho at Pho Hung is around 60,000 VND, practically free at around $3.00 USD. Pho Hung's main franchise rival is Pho 24 who started the push for cleanliness & front kitchen design however Pho Hung beats them in price.
 
One thing I liked in particular is they have small one person tables at the franchise on Nguyen Chi Phuong road in District 10 near Cholon. You know the feeling when you duck into somewhere by yourself just to have your go-to comfort food, sitting at a small compact & private one person table feels really good. Having the empty space for four people at a bigger table somehow magnifies the loneliness but with the sweet one person table you can ignore everyone else & sit there in peace to stare at women..…I mean with all your thoughts to yourself.
